A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete text, equations, ten figures, Table 1, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Wikipedia co-occurrence analyses and synthetic-model simulations, including analogy accuracy, spectra, and robustness experiments in Figures 1–3 and 6–10.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical analyses and simulations, including the supplementary experiments in Appendix A4.

M1.justification: New Appendix A5 adds a generative-model variant with interactions between different attributes, parameterized by symmetric couplings s(k,k') and word-dependent normalization factors. This is a restricted extension; the original model and spectral embedding procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Wikipedia data, Mikolov analogy benchmark, and synthetic scenarios. Added discussion of non-English corpora and LLM embeddings introduces no evaluations on those populations or models.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same M versus log(M) embedding comparisons and pruning controls. Newly cited research does not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The top-1 accuracy definition, 10,000-word Wikipedia vocabulary, logarithm regularizer, synthetic dimensions, noise settings, and sparsification procedures are unchanged. Appendix A5 introduces no experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The noise, vocabulary sparsification, pair-removal, semantic-strength, and embedding-dimension experiments remain unchanged in Figures 2–3 and 6–10. Appendix A5 supplies a theoretical extension without adding a robustness experiment.

E5.justification: The versions retain identical standard-deviation reporting and corresponding replicate counts, including 50 realizations for several spectral/accuracy analyses, 10 for noise and pair-removal experiments, and 20 for vocabulary sparsification.

E6.justification: The plotted results, result entries, and reported empirical findings match throughout the main text and Appendix A4. No numerical corrections, additional empirical outcomes, or changed rankings were found.

T1.justification: Appendix A5 adds Equations 31–33, extending the PMI decomposition to a non-diagonal attribute-interaction matrix and arguing for rank at most d+1 and preserved analogies. The derivation uses symmetric attribute probabilities and a small-coupling normalization approximation. Existing proofs and derivations are retained.

C1.justification: Contribution (3) and the Discussion broaden the robustness claim to include correlations between semantic attributes. The abstract and the central claims about spectral emergence of analogies remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A5 explains that interactions can produce eigenvectors combining multiple attributes while preserving the analogy structure within its approximation. The Discussion adds context dependence, fact retrieval, and a proposed route to testing the theory using static LLM embeddings. Existing polysemy and hierarchy limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit GitHub repository link for code, Wikipedia co-occurrence statistics, and figures, previously described only as supplementary materials. The disclosed H100 hardware and under-150-minute simulation budget are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on non-English embeddings, relation decoding in transformers, and reductions of contextual representations to static embeddings. The central positioning against latent Euclidean-space theories remains unchanged. Preprint/publication versions of existing citations do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: Changes include clearer notation definitions and appendix pointers, localized related-work and Discussion edits, affiliation corrections, a funding acknowledgment, and Appendix A5. The overall narrative and existing section organization are retained.

P2.justification: All ten figures and Table 1 retain their displays and captions. Limited layout changes include the author block and text reflow around existing figures, with the Limitations section moving onto page 10; there is no visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Appendix A5 provides a useful, bounded relaxation of attribute independence, while clearer explanations, additional research context, and explicit repository access information improve the paper. The extension relies on symmetry and a small-coupling approximation, limiting the broader robustness claim. The original empirical evidence remains intact and unchanged.
